title: Deployment Ramp Review and Hotpatch Notes - Week of 2026-03-09
content:
Meeting date: 2026-03-11
Attendees: Aisha Gomez (chair), Liam Chen, Priya Nair, Ethan Morales, Sofia Park, Marco Ruiz (SRE), Jen Walsh (QA)
Purpose: Weekly checkpoint for active release ramp, coordinate hotpatch window, and agree on changelog entries for the coming deploy.

Summary:
- Release window: Target full rollout for train 2026.03.15 (primary region us-west-2). Canary starting 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC.
- Current train composition: model-serving v2.7.1, runtime 1.14.0, autoscaler changes (feature flag: enable-burst-throttle).
- Hotpatches this week: two urgent fixes were created (see tickets RLD-1423, RLD-1430). Both are low-risk kernel selection fixes but require db migration guard on Dedicated clusters.

Detailed notes:
1) Canary plan and metrics to watch
   - Canary cohort: 1% traffic to us-west-2 (10 machines), health checks every 30s.
   - KPIs: 99th percentile latency, error rate (4xx/5xx), cache hit rate, per-token cost estimate.
   - Thresholds to abort canary: >5x baseline 99p latency OR error rate >0.5% sustained for 3 minutes.
   - Owners: Priya (metrics dashboard), Marco (SRE gating).

2) Hotpatch coordination
   - RLD-1423 (hotfix): fix for KV cache invalidation on long-lived streams. Patch deployed to staging at 2026-03-10 18:40 UTC. QA validation passed for short traces. Risk: may affect existing prefix-cache entries for Dedicated customers.
   - RLD-1430 (hotfix): selection of fp16 kernel on A100 when sequence length >4096 produced token corruption in edge cases. Patch includes additional runtime assertion and fallback to fp32 for affected paths.
   - Deployment approach: apply to canary nodes first, observe for 1 hour, then staggered rollout to remaining canary machines, then to 25% of production.
   - Required action: Add migration guard to Dedicated pools to prevent automatic rollout until customer opt-in (assigned: Ethan).

3) Changelog draft (for release notes):
   - user-facing: Improved long-stream reliability (KV cache fixes), reduced token corruption risk on long-sequence workloads, updated autoscaler behavior under burst.
   - internal ops notes: New runtime assertion added for kernel selection; customers on Dedicated may see throttling unless they opt in to new autoscaler flag.
   - Docs owner: Jen (QA + docs collab) to prepare short explainer and troubleshooting steps.

4) Risk register and mitigation
   - Risk: Dedicated customers could experience increased tail latency if autoscaler flag flips unexpectedly. Mitigation: default flag off for Dedicated; manual enable via console after compatibility check. (Action: Aisha to update rollout config)
   - Risk: Migration guard omission could trigger state divergence for prefix caches. Mitigation: add CI smoke test for cache state and require customer acceptance window. (Action: Liam to add smoke test ticket in infra repo)

5) Post-deploy validation checklist
   - Verify canary KPIs using metrics dashboard (Priya).
   - Run end-to-end smoke on Hosted and Dedicated sample tenants (Ethan).
   - Confirm no error patterns in tracing for last-token generation (Marco).
   - Sanity run of billing estimation script to ensure per-token cost unchanged (SRE-run).

6) Rollback plan and SLAs
   - If abort conditions met, immediate rollback to runtime 1.13.8. Staging rollback validated; production rollback playbook drafted in repo PR #987.
   - Communication: Exec and Customer Success notify list established (release-ops@redwood.ai).

Open action items (owner - due):
- Aisha - update rollout-configuration to keep autoscaler flag off for Dedicated by default - due 2026-03-12.
- Ethan - implement Dedicated migration guard and coordinate with solutions-eng for opt-in UX - due 2026-03-13.
- Liam - add cache-state smoke test and link to PR in infra - due 2026-03-14.
- Priya - prepare canary dashboard and alert runbook (include thresholds) - due 2026-03-12.
- Jen - draft user-facing changelog and short troubleshooting guide - due 2026-03-13.

Notes and follow-ups:
- We observed intermittent 99p latency spikes in staging correlated to a kernel selection path when sequence length >8192; extra telemetry added this morning to narrow host-specific signatures.
- Customer impact: No active incidents reported; two Dedicated customers agreed to be early opt-ins for expanded canary workloads (contact: legal-ops signed).
- Next check-in: 2026-03-13 02:30 UTC for pre-canary readiness.

Appendix: quick links and references:
- Jira RLD-1423: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/RLD-1423
- Jira RLD-1430: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/RLD-1430
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/987
- Release plan: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/2026-03-Release-Plan

Notes to self (informal):
- Remember to double-check Dedicated UX for manual opt-in flow — solutions-engineering said they’ll want a short canned message for CSMs.
- Consider a temporary metric: % of streams with fallback-to-fp32 to quantify exposure.

End of notes.
